correctness.rationale: Routh–Hurwitz κ(2κλ+v²)>κ v² implies all poles stable; numerator cancellation impossible since s=−κ not a root and other common root would be purely imaginary. At a repeated cubic root write poles −x,−x,−t x with t>0; coefficient matching yields K(t)=(t+2)^3/(t+1)^2 and w(t)=t(t+2)^3/(t+1)^4. Independent SymPy exact expansion confirms p(z)=(z+x)^2(z+tx) along curve. Derivatives w′=−2(t−1)(t+2)^2/(t+1)^5, K′=(t−1)(t+2)^2/(t+1)^3 give one/two/no fold regimes and unique t=1 cusp K=27/4,w=27/16 with cubic (z+9/4)^3. Cusp inversion F=e^(−9T/4)[1+(9/4+3sqrt3 i a/4)T+(27/16)(1+i sqrt3 a)T²]. Independently symbolically matched derivative of |F|² to the negative factor −27/512 e^(−9T/2)T(9T+4)[(1−a²)(36T+16)+(27+81a²)T²] for T>0, |a|<=1. Thus all-bias strict monotonicity holds at triple pole but not claimed elsewhere. No finite experiment used to establish global discriminant topology.
